analysis.investment_thesis: Allied Blenders and Distillers is priced as a premium consumer brand (P/B 10.62x, P/E 59.8x) yet delivered near-zero net profits for four consecutive years — INR 1-3 Cr on revenues exceeding INR 3,000 Cr — before a sudden jump to INR 195 Cr in FY2025 coinciding with a large equity infusion. Mr. Graham sees nothing but a speculative story priced for perfection with no proven earning power to justify the premium.
key_strengths: Officer's Choice brand has genuine market presence as one of India's best-selling whisky labels, suggesting some consumer franchise
ROCE of 21.1% and ROE of 20% in FY2025 look attractive, but these metrics rest on a single year of real profitability
Debt reduction trend from FY2020 to FY2023 shows some management discipline before recent leverage re-acceleration
key_risks: Revenue growth of only 3.3% CAGR over 5 years — below India's nominal GDP growth — in a consumer-facing business is deeply unimpressive
The entire valuation thesis rests on FY2025 profitability; prior four years showed INR 1-3 Cr net profit on INR 3,000+ Cr revenues
P/B of 10.62x means the investor pays INR 10.62 for every INR 1 of net assets — among the most extreme premiums in any Graham analysis
red_flags: Near-zero net profits (INR 1-3 Cr) for FY2022-FY2024 on INR 3,000+ Cr revenues — the business was barely surviving, not thriving
FY2025 operating cash flow collapsed to -INR 678 Cr despite a reported INR 195 Cr net profit — a deeply concerning divergence
Equity reserves quadrupled in FY2025 (INR 358 Cr → INR 1,502 Cr) suggesting a large capital raise; IPO-era pricing with seller advantage
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Allied Blenders is precisely the type of company I warned about in The Intelligent Investor: a business with a recognizable brand name whose investment merits are exhausted by the premium the market demands for that name. At P/B 10.62x, investors are paying INR 10.62 for every rupee of book value. For this premium to be justified, the business must demonstrate sustained high returns on equity — which it emphatically has not, having earned INR 1-3 Cr net profit annually for four years on revenues exceeding INR 3,000 Cr.

The FY2025 results deserve particular scrutiny. Net profit leapt to INR 195 Cr while operating cash flow simultaneously crashed to -INR 678 Cr — a divergence of nearly INR 873 Cr that demands explanation. Simultaneously, equity reserves quadrupled, consistent with a recent IPO or large equity raise. The seller — whether original promoters or underwriting banks — knows far more than the buyer at this juncture. At P/E 59.8x on first-year-of-real-profitability earnings, I can only classify this as pure speculation. I want no part of it.
